p: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The drainpipes [shittin]
were created from the six days of Creation,
as it is stated:
“The hidden of your thighs are like the links of a chain, … the handiwork of a skilled workman” … “The hidden of your thighs”; … these are the drainpipes

“The hidden of your thighs are like the links of a chain, the handiwork of a skilled workman” (Song of Songs 7:2). The Gemara interprets the verse homiletically: “The hidden of your thighs”; these are the drainpipes
“are like the links of a chain [ḥala’im]”; they are hollow [meḥolalin] and descend to the depths; “the handiwork of a skilled workman”; this is the handiwork of the Holy One, Blessed be He.

p: It was taught
Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok said:
There was a small gap between the ramp and the altar west of the ramp,
and once in seventy years young priests
descend there and gather from there the congealed wine … which resembled round cakes of … figs. … They would
descend there and gather from there the congealed wine left over from the libations that set over time, which resembled round cakes of dried and pressed figs. They would
come and burn it in sanctity
as it is stated:
“In sanctity shall you pour a libation of strong drink unto the Lord”
